chunks: He said: Abul Hasan 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Hubaysh al-Katib reported to me from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Za'farani, who reported from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Muhammad ibn Zakariyya, from Abdullah ibn al-Dahhak, from Hisham ibn Muhammad, who said:

When news of the assassination of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, reached Amirul Mu'mineen, peace be upon him, he wrote to Malik ibn al-Harith al-Ashtar, may Allah bless him with mercy, who was then residing at Nasibayn: "You are surely among those from whom I seek help to establish the religion, and to crush the arrogance of the sinful, and to fortify the threatened frontier. I had appointed Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, may Allah bless him with mercy, to govern Egypt, but the rebels attacked him. He was inexperienced in warfare and was martyred, may Allah bless him with mercy. So come to me that we may look into the affairs of Egypt, and appoint in your place a trustworthy and sincere person from your companions." Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, appointed Shabib ibn Amir al-Azdi to succeed him, and proceeded until he arrived before Amirul Mu'mineen, peace be upon him. He discussed the situation of Egypt with him and informed him about its people. He said: "There is no one for this assignment but you, so go forth. Even if I do not counsel you, I trust your judgment. Seek assistance from Allah in what concerns you. Mix severity with gentleness, and be gentle when gentleness serves better, and be resolute in severity when nothing avails you but severity." Malik al-Ashtar, may Allah be pleased with him, went to his quarters and prepared for the journey to Egypt. Amirul Mu'mineen, peace be upon him, sent ahead of him a letter to the people of Egypt: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Peace be upon you. I praise Allah before you, the One besides Whom there is no god, and I beseech Him to send blessings upon His Prophet Muhammad and his progeny. I have sent to you a servant from the servants of Allah who does not sleep in the days of fear, nor does he recoil from the enemies fearing any disaster. He is among the most valiant of Allah's servants, and the noblest in lineage. He is more threatening to the transgressors than blazing fire, and the farthest of people from defilement or shame. He is Malik ibn al-Harith al-Ashtar, neither of blunted tooth nor dulled edge. He is patient in caution, composed in war, possessing original judgment and agreeable patience. Listen to him and obey his command. If he orders you to march forth, march. If he orders you to stay, stay. For he does not advance nor retreat except by my command. I have preferred him for you over myself, as sincere counsel for you and as firm resolve against your enemy. May Allah guard you with guidance, and keep you steadfast with taqwa, and may He bless us and you with what He loves and is pleased with. And peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings." When Malik al-Ashtar prepared to depart for Egypt, the spies of Mu'awiyah in Iraq wrote to inform him. This greatly distressed Mu'awiyah, for he had coveted Egypt and knew that if al-Ashtar reached it, it would be lost to him, and al-Ashtar was more formidable to him than the son of Abi Bakr. So he sent word to a chief who collected revenue at al-Qulzum, telling him that 'Ali had sent al-Ashtar to Egypt, and if he eliminated him, he would grant him the revenue of his district for life, and to plot his killing by any means possible. Then Mu'awiyah gathered the people of Syria and said to them: "'Ali has sent al-Ashtar to Egypt, so come and let us pray to Allah against him that He may relieve us of his affair." Then he prayed and they prayed with him. Al-Ashtar traveled until he reached al-Qulzum. That chief received him and greeted him and said: "I am a man who pays the revenue, and you and your companions have a right to the produce of my land. So be my guest and let me attend to your affairs, feed your companions, and provide fodder for your animals, and count that for me from the revenue." Al-Ashtar stayed with him, and the chief served him and his companions with all they needed. He brought them food in which he had secretly placed poisoned honey. When al-Ashtar drank it, it killed him and he died from it. When Mu'awiyah received the news, he gathered the people of Syria and told them: "Rejoice! Allah Most High has answered your prayers and has relieved you of al-Ashtar and caused his death." They rejoiced and were glad. When news of al-Ashtar's death reached Amirul Mu'mineen, peace be upon him, he sighed and grieved over him, saying: "What an excellent man Malik was! Had he been a mountain, he would have been its greatest pillar, and had he been from stone, he would have been solid. By Allah, your death will shake the world, and over one like you the mourners should weep." Then he said: "Indeed, we belong to Allah and to Him we return. All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the Worlds. I consider him my sacrifice before You, for his death is among the calamities of the age. May Allah have mercy on Malik, for he fulfilled his pledge and completed his appointed term and met his Lord. While we have resolved to bear every calamity after our bereavement of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his progeny, for that was the greatest calamity."

key_terms.الأشتر: Al-Ashtar - Malik ibn al-Harith al-Ashtar al-Nakha'i, one of the most loyal companions of Imam Ali, known for his military prowess and leadership
key_terms.القلزم: Al-Qulzum - a port town near the northern tip of the Red Sea (modern-day Suez area), where al-Ashtar was poisoned
key_terms.دهقان: Dihqan - a local chief or landowner, particularly used for Persian or non-Arab notables who managed agricultural estates
key_terms.نصيبين: Nasibayn - a city in Upper Mesopotamia (modern-day Nusaybin in southeastern Turkey), where al-Ashtar was stationed

ai.seo_question: How was Malik al-Ashtar assassinated and what did Imam Ali say about him?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts how Imam Ali (AS) appointed Malik al-Ashtar as governor of Egypt after the killing of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, writing him a letter of appointment and a separate letter to the Egyptians praising al-Ashtar's virtues. It then describes how Mu'awiyah conspired to have al-Ashtar poisoned at al-Qulzum during his journey to Egypt, and concludes with Imam Ali's deeply moving eulogy upon learning of al-Ashtar's death, comparing him to an immovable mountain and quoting the Quranic verse of patience.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 4. He said: Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Hubaysh al-katib reported to me from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali al-Za’farani, who reported from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Muhammad ibn Zakariyya, from Abdullah ibn al-Dhahhak, from Hisham ibn Muhammad, who said:

When news of the assassination of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, reached Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, he wrote to Malik ibn al-Harith al-Ashtar, may Allah bless him with mercy, who was then residing at Nasibayn. (He wrote): "You are surely among those from whom I seek help to keep the banner of Islam high and to crush the haughtiness of the disobedient and to fortify the threatened borderline. I had appointed Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, may Allah bless him with mercy, to govern Egypt, but the rebels attacked him and as he was inexperienced about warfare, he was martyred - may Allah bless him with mercy. Now, come over to me so that we may look into the matter concerning Egypt, and appoint in your place a reliable, sane person from your companions." Then Malik - may Allah be pleased with him, appointed Shabib ibn Amir al-Azadi to succeed him, and proceeded till he arrived to meet Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him. Then he (i.e. ‘Ali) explained to him the situation in Egypt and informed him about its people. Then he said: "There is no one for this assignment except you, so be ready to go. And if there is anything, about which I have not guided you, you will depend upon your judgement and seek assistance from Allah for your intention. (In your dealing with them), mix severity and harshness with tenderness and gentleness, and be friendly for as long as friendliness serves the purpose. And be resolute when there is no alternative to severity." He said: Then Malik al-Ashtar - may Allah be pleased with him, rose and prepared for his journey to Egypt. And ‘Ali, peace be upon him, sent a letter to the people of Egypt, before (Malik) arrived there: "In the name of Allah, Most Merciful, Most Benevolent, I praise Allah, none to be worshipped but He; and beseech Allah to bless His Prophet, Muhammad and his progeny. Surely, I have sent unto you a servant from the servants of Allah, who does not sleep in the days of fear and does not recoil from the enemy fearing any disaster. He is from the strongest among His servants and the noblest; and to the transgressors, more threatening than the burning fire. And from ignorance and blemish, he is the farthest. He is Malik ibn al-Harith al-Ashtar, neither a cutting tooth nor a blunted edge. He is patient amid threats, calm and composed at the time of war. He has an original judgement and an agreeable patience. So listen to him and obey him. If he commands you to march forth, march, and if commands you to halt, halt. For he does not advance or halt except by my order. I have sent him to you in spite of my need for him, for the sake of your welfare and because of my deep concern about your adversaries. May Allah guard and protect you with guidance and keep you steadfast with Taqwa. May He bless us and you with what He likes and loves. May peace and mercy of Allah and His Blessing be upon you." When Malik al-Ashtar completed his preparations for journey to Egypt, the spies of Mu’awiyah from Iraq wrote to inform him. He was very much distressed, because he had his eyes set on Egypt. He knew that he would lose Egypt if al-Ashtar arrived there and to him al-Ashtar was a more powerful person than the son of Abu Bakr. So he contacted a chief who paid the revenue at a place called al-Qulzum, informing him that ‘Ali (as) has appointed al-Ashtar to govern Egypt and if you got rid of him on my behalf, I shall gift away the revenue to you for as long as you live. So plan to kill him in every way possible. Then Mu’awiyah collected the people of Syria and said: "Verily, ‘Ali has sent al-Ashtar to Egypt. Come and let us pray to Allah that He may relieve us of him." Then he prayed, and so did the people with him. Al-Ashtar travelled on till he came to al-Qulzum. The chief received him and greeted him and then said: "I am among those who is liable to pay the revenue. And you and your companions have a right upon all that grows on my land. So be my guest and allow me to serve you and your companions and let your animals freely graze on my land, and I will count it from my liability." So, al-Ashtar became his guest and he served him (al-Ashtar) and his companions for all their needs. And he brought to them food, including some honey, which had poison. When al-Ashtar drank from that honey, it killed him and he died because of that. Mu’awiyah got the news, so he collected the people of Syria and said: "Happy tidings for you! Allah, Most High, has answered your prayers; has relieved you of him and has killed him." They rejoiced. And when the news of Ashtar’s death assailed Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, he sighed and grieved, saying: "What an excellent man Malik was! Had he been a mountain, he would have been its firm rock, and had he been from stone, he would have been solid. By Allah, some men in the world will be placated by his death; but it behaves for the mourners to mourn over him." Then he said: "We are for Allah and unto Him shall we return; and all praise to Allah, the Lord of all Universe. I shall seek reward from You for this sacrifice, for surely, his death is among the greatest worldly calamities. May Allah bless Malik with mercy; no doubt, he faithfully dispersed his charge and completed the appointed term (of life) and met his Creator; while we have reconciled ourselves to forbear every adversity after being bereaved of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, for that was the greatest calamity."
